post_message: “This survey is a wake-up call,” says Dr. Lucica Ditiu, Executive Director of Stop TB Partnership. “We cannot assume that people will simply welcome a new TB vaccine when it becomes available."   A first-ever joint survey from the Stop TB Partnership and the Sabin Vaccine Institute highlights the need for robust preparedness before new vaccines become available in 2029 to protect against tuberculosis (TB), the world’s top infectious killer.  A concerning 67% of the more than 1,400 respondents from 86 countries say they have heard little or nothing about new TB vaccines that will be available soon. Two-thirds of the respondents identified low community awareness of the vaccines as the biggest barrier to vaccine roll-out, followed by circulating misinformation and cost or affordability  Tuberculosis causes an estimated 1.25 million deaths each year. The burden is very high as an estimated 2 billion people are infected with TB and the disease is increasingly resistant to antibiotics.  The joint survey looked at readiness in Stop TB’s TB communities, international and technical organizations, government programs, research and funding agencies, NGOs, and survivors and among Sabin’s Boost global community of immunization professionals at local and national levels. About two-thirds of the respondents work in high-burden TB countries.  “Reaching people who need this vaccine requires collaboration between tuberculosis and immunization communities, including joint planning, shared advocacy, country-level cooperation, resource mobilization, and continued learning,” says Dr. Rebecca Martin, President of Global Immunization at Sabin. “These survey findings allow global partners, governments, healthcare workers, and community organizations to address the identified needs and lay the groundwork for success.”  See the full survey results⤵️ https://ow.ly/RUx651025FG

post_message: VIEW-hub, a tool developed by the International Vaccine Access Center at Johns Hopkins BSPH, is a valuable resource for country decision makers and the broader immunization community.  We are excited to see it host resources developed through Sabin’s #Hexavalent Vaccine (Switch) Assessment Consortium (HeVAC), with a new page bringing together information and practical resources on hexavalent vaccines in one accessible location.   Many of these resources were co-created with immunization program leaders from countries that had completed the switch, were preparing for introduction, or were considering applying for support.  As more countries consider the switch to a hexavalent vaccine — a six-in-one shot that allows for fewer injections, simplified schedules, logistical efficiencies, and stronger integration of polio vaccination into routine services — these materials can help them learn from peer experiences, anticipate common challenges, and plan for successful introduction. The Sabin Vaccine Institute continues to unlock the full benefits of vaccines to protect people everywhere. We turn innovation into impact: developing vaccines, responding to vaccine-preventable outbreaks, and generating data that informs country decision making around deploying immunization to save lives.

post_message: It was wonderful to connect with #GlobalHPVConsortium partners and meet new colleagues at #IPVS2026 in Athens last week.  The team shared findings from our Male HPV Vaccination Working Group's Male HPV Vaccination Global Landscaping Survey. Working group co-chair David Winterflood of NOMAN is an Island: Race to End HPV joined Meredith Dockery from Sabin to present data from the survey's 225 responses from all six World Health Organization regions.  The survey explored what shapes consideration of HPV vaccination for boys and men. Respondents identified evidence on HPV-related diseases in males and updated global guidance as important policy drivers, while vaccine price, competing priorities and sustainable financing remain significant challenges.   More to come on the survey results! Thank you to everyone who participated in the survey and to those who visited our poster. Already looking forward to #IPVS2027!

post_message: “This survey is a wake-up call,” says Dr. Lucica Ditiu, Executive Director of Stop TB Partnership. “We cannot assume that people will simply welcome a new TB vaccine when it becomes available."   A first-ever joint survey from the Stop TB Partnership and the Sabin Vaccine Institute highlights the need for robust preparedness before new vaccines become available in 2029 to protect against tuberculosis (TB), the world’s top infectious killer.  A concerning 67% of the more than 1,400 respondents from 86 countries say they have heard little or nothing about new TB vaccines that will be available soon. Two-thirds of the respondents identified low community awareness of the vaccines as the biggest barrier to vaccine roll-out, followed by circulating misinformation and cost or affordability  Tuberculosis causes an estimated 1.25 million deaths each year. The burden is very high as an estimated 2 billion people are infected with TB and the disease is increasingly resistant to antibiotics.  The joint survey looked at readiness in Stop TB’s TB communities, international and technical organizations, government programs, research and funding agencies, NGOs, and survivors and among Sabin’s Boost global community of immunization professionals at local and national levels. About two-thirds of the respondents work in high-burden TB countries.  “Reaching people who need this vaccine requires collaboration between tuberculosis and immunization communities, including joint planning, shared advocacy, country-level cooperation, resource mobilization, and continued learning,” says Dr. Rebecca Martin, President of Global Immunization at Sabin. “These survey findings allow global partners, governments, healthcare workers, and community organizations to address the identified needs and lay the groundwork for success.”  See the full survey results⤵️ https://ow.ly/jBeL51024wy
